title: Method chaining and the fluent interface

videos.script: Some code reads like a sentence. New receipt, line, line, print. This lesson is about how a class makes that possible, and when it is worth doing. {{this}} The trick is one line: a method that returns the object it was called on. StringBuilder does it, and a receipt class of your own does it in three. {{void}} A setter that returns nothing breaks the chain, and the compiler says so. {{builder}} Then the builder. A loan has a book and a member that it must have, and a period and a note that it may have. A builder takes them one at a time and checks them all at the end. {{immutable}} Last, chains on objects that never change. Every call returns a new object, and the commonest bug is forgetting to keep it. A renewed due date that did not move, and the compiler said nothing.
